html:
A Baoule chief, doctor and cocoa planter who led Ivory Coast from before independence in 1960 until his death in 1993.

In 1944 he organised African planters against colonial rules that favoured whites. Elected to the French parliament in 1945, he passed the 1946 law that abolished forced labour in the French colonies, and he founded the African Democratic Rally, the main party of French West Africa. As president he kept close ties to France, welcomed foreign capital and migrant workers, and the cocoa boom made the country rich for a time. He ruled a one-party state until 1990 and built the Basilica of Yamoussoukro in his home town. His death opened the struggle that led to the civil war.
